status_summary: Executive Order 14182 (signed 2025-01-24) revoked two 2022 orders and directs OMB guidance to end use of federal funds for elective abortion consistent with the Hyde Amendment, and State's final rule effective 2026-02-26 applies a Mexico City Policy award term to non-military foreign assistance. Section 71113 of Public Law 119-21 (2025-07-04) barred Medicaid payments to certain abortion providers for one year, which a Massachusetts federal court preliminarily enjoined as to Planned Parenthood Federation members on 2025-07-28; reports say it expired on 2026-07-04 without an extension. FDA's review of the mifepristone safety program was announced in September 2025 and had produced no change as of the status report filed on 2026-10-07, which projects study results by mid-December 2026 and a report by March 2027, and the Supreme Court on 2026-05-14 left current dispensing rules in place while litigation continues. On adoption, the 2025 reconciliation law expanded the adoption tax credit and a November 2025 proclamation highlighted adoption and foster care; no new federal statutory protection for the unborn has been enacted.

timeline.event: President signs Executive Order 14182, Enforcing the Hyde Amendment (published 2025-01-31): it states a policy to end use of federal taxpayer funds for elective abortion consistent with the Hyde Amendment, revokes Executive Orders 14076 and 14079 of 2022 and directs OMB to issue implementing guidance. It creates no enforceable rights.

Public Law 119-21 is signed; section 71113 bars federal Medicaid payments for one year to nonprofit essential community providers primarily engaged in family planning that provide abortions outside narrow exceptions and received more than $800,000 in Medicaid payments in fiscal year 2023.
timeline.source: U.S. District Court, District of Massachusetts

timeline.event: In Planned Parenthood Federation of America v. Kennedy the District of Massachusetts (Judge Talwani) grants a preliminary injunction against enforcing section 71113 against Federation members, finding plaintiffs likely to succeed on First Amendment association, equal protection and bill of attainder claims; the court states it is not requiring federal funding of abortion.
timeline.source: U.S. District Court, District of Massachusetts

timeline.event: Proclamation 10992 (signed 2025-11-17) designates November 2025 National Adoption Month, credits the 2025 reconciliation law with making the adoption tax credit more accessible and references an executive order on supporting youth in and leaving foster care.

State publishes the final rule Protecting Life in Foreign Assistance (2 CFR part 602, effective 2026-02-26): an award term bars foreign NGOs and international organizations from providing or promoting abortion as family planning, applies to U.S. NGOs' funded programs and to non-military foreign assistance, and implements the 2025-01-24 Mexico City Policy memorandum.

In Louisiana v. FDA the Western District of Louisiana stays the case for six months while FDA reviews the mifepristone safety program and orders FDA to file a status report on the review by 2026-10-07; current dispensing rules remain in place.
The Supreme Court blocks a Fifth Circuit order that would have reinstated in-person mifepristone dispensing, leaving current FDA rules in place while the case returns to the Fifth Circuit.

The one-year section 71113 Medicaid payment prohibition ends by its terms; local reports say Planned Parenthood health centers resumed Medicaid billing for non-abortion services and no extension had been enacted.

In Louisiana v. FDA the federal defendants file the court-ordered status report: FDA is running a mifepristone safety study and expects results by mid-December 2026 and a final study report by March 2027, while separately reviewing the REMS program and pending citizen petitions; no REMS change is reported.
timeline.source: U.S. District Court, Western District of Louisiana

title: Protect the unborn through legislation, federal powers, funding bans and adoption support
uncertainties: The Foreword asks for the strongest protections Congress will support, so there is no fixed end state. The statutory text of section 71113 was read through the court memorandum, not the public law. The reported First Circuit action and the plaintiffs' dismissal are known only from a secondary summary in c14-07 and are not used here. The expiry of the payment prohibition rests on a local news report. The 2026-04-07 stay order in Louisiana v. FDA is known from a news report and from the recital in the government's 2026-10-07 status report, not from the order itself. Whether the executive branch has complied strictly with other statutory funding bans (such as in the ACA marketplace or federal employee plans) was not examined. The reported Justice Department statement of 2026-04-23 that FDA's mifepristone review was ongoing is known only from a news page of the Center for Reproductive Rights, an advocacy group, and is not confirmed by an official document; it is an unverified lead at low confidence and is not used here. The court-ordered status report was filed on 2026-10-07, according to a copy of the filing hosted by the Georgetown University litigation tracker. The adoption tax credit expansion is described by the proclamation, not read in the statute; the executive order Fostering the Future was not fetched. Related records c14-03, c14-07 and c09-04 carry more detail.
